solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Not going in right direction, as misguided Express perhaps (2,3,5,5)

blocks.note: the figurative sense: mistaken, heading for the wrong conclusion
an express is a fast train; a misguided one has been switched onto rails it should not be on

annotation.surface: A commentator scolding a newspaper, the Express, for losing its way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Express' is capitalised to look like the Daily Express newspaper; here it is a fast train, and 'perhaps' flags it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from the railway: the literal train sense in the second half grounds the figurative 'mistaken' sense in the first.

entries.clue: Old books inspiring weary expression at first glance (2,5)

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so NT takes SIGH inside it

annotation.surface: Dusty old volumes that make a reader sigh the moment they are seen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old books' begs to be OT, the Old Testament; the setter means O for old and then the New Testament, and 'inspiring' is breathing in.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to know or judge something the instant you see it, without a second look.

entries.clue: Two learners in mountainous region (5)

blocks.note: the first learner: a tyro is a beginner
the second learner: L, as on a learner driver's plate

annotation.surface: A pair of novice skiers or climbers out in the Alps.
annotation.walkthrough: One word, 'learners', is made to do two jobs in two different forms; the L plate is what British learner drivers must display.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name defined by its geography: the Alpine region straddling western Austria and northern Italy.

entries.clue: Get rid of model created with AI (9)

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

annotation.surface: A call to scrap an AI model, very much a topic of the day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a noun, the AI model; it works as a verb, shaping CREATED plus AI into the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though stronger: literally to pull out by the roots, so removal that is total.

entries.clue: Sally’s unfinished journal turned up (4)

indicators.note: a thing unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter of DIARY goes
in a down clue, turning something up reads it bottom to top

annotation.surface: A girl called Sally finds her half-written diary.
annotation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a name; it is a sudden attack, as when troops sally out.
annotation.definitionFit: A military sense: a sally is a sudden sortie out of a besieged position against the attackers.

entries.clue: Singer’s glass of beer in the evening? (8)

blocks.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

annotation.surface: A pub singer having a pint after the evening's show.
annotation.walkthrough: The singer is a bird, not a performer, and the clue's order is reversed: the glass comes second in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: birds are 'singers' in crosswords, and this one churrs at dusk.

entries.clue: German city bank welcoming reforms at first (5)

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes them in, so the bank takes in the letter
only what comes first, the opening letter, of reforms is used

blocks.note: a bank is a row or tier, as of seats or oars

annotation.surface: A German bank opening its doors to reforms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money; it is a row set one above another.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: the old Roman city on the Moselle in western Germany.

entries.clue: Humiliation as Sam beaten badly (9)

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad, disordered state

annotation.surface: The humiliation of Sam losing heavily in some contest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As' is only a link; the fodder is the nine letters of SAM and BEATEN, and 'badly' does double duty on the surface as how Sam lost.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to abase is to lower, so this is humiliation seen as being brought down.

entries.clue: House weakness Etonian conceals (7)

indicators.note: the phrase conceals the answer inside it

blocks.note: the tail of weakness and the head of Etonian

annotation.surface: An Eton schoolboy hiding a weakness from his house at school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests an Eton boarding house; it is a legislative house. An Etonian is a pupil of Eton, the English public school.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Israel's parliament is a single legislative house.

entries.clue: Angry about king’s coursing (9)

indicators.note: one thing about another surrounds it, so STEAMING goes round the R

annotation.surface: A king furious about his hare coursing, the old field sport with greyhounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coursing' suggests the hunting sport; here it is water coursing, flowing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for liquid running: tears or rain coursing down are pouring in a stream.

entries.clue: Frivolous interlude ending thus? (5)

blocks.note: the surface wants the close of a light entertainment; the setter wants the final letter of the word interlude
'thus' asks you to describe that ending in words, and the description itself is the answer

annotation.surface: A light, silly interval that closes a show.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'interlude' as a word, not an event: it ends in an E, and 'in an E', run together, is a word for silly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: inane talk is empty and silly, as frivolous talk is.

entries.clue: French female left in charge (6)

annotation.surface: A Frenchwoman who has been put in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French female' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'French'.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical synonym: Gaul was the Roman name for the land that became France.

entries.clue: Increasingly blunt head of state revealing all (8)

indicators.note: the head is the top, so the first letter of state

blocks.note: stark = blunt, so more blunt is the comparative

annotation.surface: A head of state growing ever franker and telling everything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of state' looks like a president; it gives only S. The answer is British slang for stark naked.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: someone with nothing on is showing everything, which the surface passes off as candour.

entries.clue: Grief consuming British family (6)

definitions.note: 'family' is used adjectivally, as in family loyalty

indicators.note: what consumes something swallows it whole, so TRIAL takes the B inside it

blocks.note: a trial is a trouble, a grief

annotation.surface: A British family eaten up by grief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Family' looks like the noun at the end of the surface; it works as an adjective, as in family ties.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjectival sense: loyalties owed to one's kin group are family ones, a tribe being an extended family.

entries.clue: Establish seat of learning (9)

blocks.note: a verb: to set up, found
a noun: a college or academy

annotation.surface: Founding a university.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one action; it splits into a verb and a noun that share a spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain: the verb means to set up, the noun a place of study or research.

entries.clue: Supremely inept cowboy cut short time on eastern seaboard (8)

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so GAUCHO loses its last letter

blocks.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy, minus the O
Eastern Standard Time on the US east coast

annotation.surface: A hopeless cowboy stuck on the US east coast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cowboy' suggests an American; the gaucho rides the South American pampas. EST is the time zone of the US eastern seaboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A superlative of a French borrowing: gauche, literally left-handed, means awkward, so 'supremely' matches the -EST.

entries.clue: Accurate cast netting small shrimps? (9)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into a new form, as metal is cast
the rearranged letters take in S like a catch

annotation.surface: A precise throw of a net that brings in some small shrimps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' and 'netting' both belong to the fishing picture; the question mark flags shrimps as one example of the class.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: shrimps belong to this class, along with crabs and lobsters.

entries.clue: PM’s daughter a citizen of foreign power (8)

blocks.note: a citizen of Israel, a foreign power

annotation.surface: A prime minister whose daughter holds foreign citizenship, a political scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'PM's daughter' reads as a person related to a PM; the 's is 'is', so PM is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Benjamin Disraeli was twice Victoria's Prime Minister.

entries.clue: New bats I destroyed — put them here? (5,3)

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A cricketer who has just smashed his new bats wondering where to throw them.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: broken bats are what you would throw away, and the question mark admits the stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: 'them' points back to the destroyed bats, and a bin is where rubbish goes.

entries.clue: Conflict upset Green Party’s provisions? (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns RAW upside down

blocks.note: the food a party lays on

annotation.surface: A row that has upset the Green Party's policy provisions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Green Party' looks like one name; it splits, with Green giving RAW. Taken together, raw fare is also the kind of food a Green might eat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: armed struggle between nations or groups.

entries.clue: I disapprove of short skirts (3-3)

indicators.note: each skirt is short of its last letter

blocks.note: the first skirt: a ballet tutu, lacking its final U
the second skirt, curtailed the same way

annotation.surface: A prude frowning at miniskirts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short skirts' suggests minis; they are ballet tutus, both curtailed, and the plural is what gives two of them.
annotation.definitionFit: An interjection standing for a sentence: the clicking sound people make to say they disapprove.

entries.clue: Partners getting into property conveyance (7)

indicators.note: partners getting into a thing end up inside it, so NS sits within TRAIT

blocks.note: North and South are partners at bridge
a property is a characteristic, a trait

annotation.surface: A couple buying into a property, with the legal conveyancing to sort out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Property' and 'conveyance' both read as house-buying; property here is a characteristic, and conveyance is transport.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the transport sense: the carrying of people or goods from place to place.

entries.clue: Has fun in Rolls, going round India (8)

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so the rolls surround India's letter

blocks.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone enjoying themselves being driven round India in a Rolls-Royce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' is capitalised to suggest the car; it is lists of names.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym, if a rowdier one: to roister is to revel noisily.

entries.clue: Nurse’s nice surprise (5)

blocks.note: a verb here: to give medical care to a patient

annotation.surface: A nurse pleasantly surprised.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' reads as a noun; it is the verb, to tend, and the 's is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both plain: to tend a patient medically, and an unlooked-for pleasure.

entries.clue: More work beginning to use revolutionary artificial intelligence corporation (6)

indicators.note: just the first letter of use
turning round, so AI POT reverses

blocks.note: a corporation is a large belly, a pot

annotation.surface: A company pushing its workers harder with a radical new AI tool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'More work' reads as extra labour; it is a work by Thomas More, the Tudor statesman. 'Corporation' is jocular old slang for a paunch.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by authorship: Thomas More's 1516 book describing an ideal island state.

entries.clue: Physicist announced part of political party’s programme (5)

indicators.note: the name is spoken, not spelt

annotation.surface: A scientist declaring one of a party's policies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Announced' reads as the physicist making a statement; it signals the sound of his name.
annotation.definitionFit: A political metaphor: a party's platform is built of planks, each one policy.

entries.clue: Writer coming out of shell in bed (4)

indicators.note: the outer letters, the shell, are removed

blocks.note: SCRIBE without its outer letters S and E

annotation.surface: A shy writer finally emerging from their shell while in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coming out of shell' reads as becoming sociable; it means the writer loses its shell.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a baby's cot with barred sides is one kind of bed.

entries.clue: Exploit a brief kiss — hope at last? (5)

indicators.note: something brief is short, so BUSS is cut short by its final letter
only the last letter of hope

blocks.note: BUSS, an old word for a kiss, cut short

annotation.surface: Someone taking advantage of a quick kiss, hoping for more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brief kiss' suggests a peck; it is BUSS, an old word for a kiss, shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to take unfair advantage of a position or trust.

entries.clue: Courts are wrong to identify union officials (9)

indicators.note: the letters are set wrong, out of order

annotation.surface: Courts wrongly identifying trade union officials.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Union officials' suggests trade unions; the union is the European Union.
annotation.definitionFit: A misdirecting description: the union is the European one, and these are its Brussels bureaucrats.

entries.clue: Source of comfort in bitter retirement times? (8,7)

definitions.text: Source of comfort in bitter retirement times?

blocks.note: the surface wants resentful; the setter wants bitterly cold
the surface wants old age after work; the setter wants the hour you retire to bed

annotation.surface: Something to console a pensioner through a hard old age.
annotation.walkthrough: Once retirement is bedtime and bitter is freezing, the source of comfort is the thing that warms the sheets.
annotation.definitionFit: A whole-clue description: a heated bed cover is what makes going to bed on a freezing night bearable.
